rounds.learn: A variable is a name that holds a value. The = sign puts the value into the name. After that, you use the name instead of the value.
rounds.task: Save your reason in a variable called goal. Then print goal.
rounds.say: Look at print(goal). No quotes. Without quotes, Python looks up the name and prints what it holds.

rounds.learn: A variable can change. If you set it again, the newest value wins.
rounds.task: Set mood to tired. Then set it to focused. Print it.
Make tool hold hammer. Change it to drill. Print it.
rounds.say: drill wins. Newest value, every time.

rounds.task: Make a variable called name that holds your name. Then print it.
rounds.hint: Two lines. name = "..." with your name in the quotes. Then print(name), with no quotes around name.

checks.msg: Make a variable called name first, with name = ...
Now print the variable itself: print(name), no quotes.

rounds.say: Hi, %out%. You just used a variable with nothing to copy from.
